text:
For a **short outage**, a power station around **300 Wh** may keep a low-wattage heat mat going for several hours. For **overnight or longer**, I’d look at a **roughly 2,000 Wh station**—especially if you’re powering a heat lamp or ceramic heat emitter.

As a rough estimate, a **24 W heat mat** plus the station’s own power use may draw about **40 W**: a 288 Wh station could last around **6–8 hours**, while a 2,073 Wh station could last roughly **two days**. A **100 W ceramic emitter running half the time** could use about **65 W including station overhead**, making that 2,073 Wh station closer to **a day**. These are estimates, not measured reptile-enclosure tests; actual runtime depends on the heater, thermostat cycling, and room temperature. ([runtime examples](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-keep-reptile-heat-on-in-a-power-outage))

Choose a station with **AC output rated above your heater’s wattage**, and keep the heater on its **thermostat**. If you tell me the heater’s wattage and how many hours you need, I can help estimate the capacity more closely. Meanwhile, insulating the enclosure and having wrapped hand warmers ready can help during a short outage. ([Petco outage guidance](https://www.petco.com/pet-education/reptile/general/caring-for-your-pet-reptiles-during-a-power-outage))
